That is exactly the shape and exactly the kind of evidence wanted here, so this is filling a gap in an established pattern, not designing a new one.
Ten distinct provisions: Minn. Const. art. IV sections 4 and 6, art. V section 1, art. VII section 6; Neb. Const. art. III sections 1, 7, 8 and 12, art. IV sections 1 and 2.
Do not answer with the date the text was retrieved or last published. That is what the corpus already has, and it is the thing that does not work.
question: For each of ten named provisions of the Minnesota and Nebraska constitutions, on what date did the provision's current words take effect, and what primary or publisher material establishes that date?

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Nineteen rows carry provisionValidity CURRENT_OBSERVATION with observedOn 2026-09-09, and all nineteen are Minnesota (6) and Nebraska (13). Their own recorded reason states the gap: the acquired publisher snapshot proves the current words on the observation date, but no claim-specific primary material in this corpus proves how far back those same words applied. The other fifty rows, across Massachusetts, Missouri, New Jersey, Nevada and Ohio, carry EXACT_INTERVAL with a real validFrom.

sourcesChecked.source: The publisher pages already acquired: revisor.mn.gov/constitution and the Nebraska Legislature's constitution pages
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: They present the constitution as it currently stands. Neither page, as acquired, states per-section when the present language was ratified or took effect.

title: When the present words of ten Minnesota and Nebraska constitutional provisions took effect
usableAnswer: A row per provision: the citation, the date the current language took effect, whether that is a ratification date or a later stated effective date, and the material that establishes it — a ratification note, an election canvass, a session-law or amendment record, or the constitution's own provision on when an amendment takes effect. Where a provision has been amended since and the current words are older or newer than the article's headline date, say which. If a provision's commencement genuinely cannot be established from available material, say that with what you checked; an honest unknown keeps the present refusal, which is the safe outcome, and is far better than a guessed date.
whyItMatters: Nobody can stand for office in Nebraska, and the Minnesota House refuses the same character the Senate accepts. The cause is not a rule and not a bug: the game will not apply a constitutional requirement to a date earlier than the day it observed the text, and the ordinary start date is 5 January 2026 while these texts were read on 9 September 2026. That discipline is right and has already caught real provenance leaks, so the repair is not to relax it. The repair is the commencement date, which is the fact the EXACT_INTERVAL rows already carry and these ten do not. With it, two states become playable without anything being assumed.
